sources.fact: LBBD Regulation 19 HTML lists CD - London Road and North Street as a site-allocation attachment.
Cabinet approval concerned publication and submission of the Local Plan, not an individual CD planning permission.
September 2018 Cabinet minutes describe redevelopment proposals for land at London Road and North Street.
The 2018 outline commercial arrangement referred to 164 build-to-rent units.
The 2018 outline plans referred to 35 percent affordable discounted-market-rent homes and ground-floor commercial space.
The minutes distinguish the former White Horse site from the adjacent Council-owned bus-layover land.
Cabinet decided on 21 January 2025 to terminate the existing development agreement route because of lack of progress.
The 2025 decision rescinded the offer of a development loan of up to 52 million pounds.
The preferred route allowed negotiation of disposal of Council interests, subject to best-consideration safeguards.
If acceptable disposal terms were not agreed, the Council could retain its majority holding and remarket the site.
Termination, disposal and remarketing governance do not prove current issued planning permission or construction completion.
No exact current residential application decision, HMLR title relation or executed overlay for the combined CD boundary was verified this wave.

examples.result: CD allocation identity is retained from official Regulation 19 HTML.
The 164-unit 2018 outline proposal is not treated as a current 2026 permission.
The 35 percent affordable reference is proposal context, not delivered tenure proof.
The 2025 termination decision supersedes the earlier development-agreement route without cancelling the allocation.
The rescinded 52 million pound loan is finance governance, not planning consent.
Disposal or remarketing options do not establish current land-title extent.
The two land interests are not merged into one legal polygon without HMLR evidence.
Promotion remains zero until exact current case, title relations and overlays are verified.
